audit.why: Corrosive Charge is 10s at rank 1 (800), Disdain 16s (475), Purge 12/9/6/3/0s (490) — it reaches zero cooldown at rank 5 — and Fear Beyond Death 100s. Disdain's 16 seconds is the punish window the page keeps gesturing at.

audit.whatIsWrong: Seven strings call the leg blasts his Q — 'his shotgun legs (Q)', 'ramping Q legs', 'percent-max-HP Q legs', 'Q-poke his short legs down'. The legs are Echoing Flames, his PASSIVE. His Q is Corrosive Charge, a ground-targeted explosion that slows.
audit.why: Riot: 'Urgot's basic attacks and Purge periodically trigger blasts of flame from his legs' (passive) and 'Fires an explosive charge at the target location, dealing physical damage and slowing enemies caught in the explosion' (Q). A player waiting for a Q cooldown to step in is waiting on the wrong thing entirely — the legs have no ability cooldown, they fire off his attacks and his W.
audit.corrected: Echoing Flames named as the passive throughout; Corrosive Charge named as the ground-targeted Q with its 10s and 800 range.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'percent-max-HP Q legs' and 'his Q shotgun legs deal percent-max-HP', repeated four times.
audit.why: Nothing in Riot's text for Echoing Flames or Corrosive Charge mentions percent maximum health — both are described as physical damage. The claim changes how a player itemises (it argues against HP), so it should not stand unsupported.
audit.corrected: Removed; replaced with what the kit does support — Purge as sustained damage and Echoing Flames firing off his attacks.

audit.whatIsWrong: Purge's targeting rule is never mentioned, and Disdain is described only as a 'flip'.
audit.why: Riot: Purge 'prioritizes enemy champions Urgot has recently struck with other abilities'. So eating a Corrosive Charge is what marks you for the barrage — that is the sequencing the mid-game advice needed. And Disdain shields him as well as flipping you, which changes the maths on trading into his engage.
audit.corrected: Purge's priority rule written into mid and wants.foe[0]; Disdain's shield into early, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0] and wants.foe[1].

audit.why: Pantheon's passive is Mortal Will; no passive shield exists.

edits.before: Urgot is a slow level 1, and you are one of the strongest — point-and-click W stun into a Q tap-reset chunks him before his shotgun legs (Q) and W Purge ramp into real DPS. Your E channel is the key tech: angle the directional block toward him to eat his W auto-attack barrage and a Q blast for free, then Q-poke his short legs down. Spike your level 2 (W+Q) and level 3 all-in hard — this is where you genuinely out-trade him. Just respect his E flip; if he lands it he repositions you onto his Q damage zones and the percent-HP starts adding up.
edits.after: Urgot is a slow level 1, and you are one of the strongest — point-and-click Shield Vault into a Comet Spear chunks him before Echoing Flames ramps. Get the names right, because they change what you dodge: the leg blasts are his passive, triggered by his attacks and by Purge, while Corrosive Charge (Q, 10s at rank 1, 800 range) is a ground-targeted explosion that slows. Aegis Assault is the key tech — face the block at him to eat a Purge barrage for free. Spike your level 2 and level 3 all-ins hard, and respect Disdain (E, 16s, 475): it shields him and hurls you back onto his damage.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 even out as Urgot's W Purge and ramping Q legs let him grind back the sustained-DPS exchanges your shields and squishy frame can't out-heal — keep poking with held long-range Q from outside his leg range rather than committing E-in all-ins. At 6 your edge isn't the 1v1, it's the map: Grand Starfall (R) lets you leave this immobile, dash-less lane and snowball another side before Urgot ever comes online. Don't sit here trying to solo-kill a tanky Urgot — take the roam.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 even out as Purge and Echoing Flames grind back the sustained exchanges your squishy frame can't out-heal — poke with the thrown Comet Spear from outside his 490 Purge range rather than committing all-ins. Note the sequencing: Purge prioritizes champions he has recently struck with another ability, so eating a Corrosive Charge marks you for the barrage. At 6 your edge is the map, not the 1v1: Grand Starfall leaves this dash-less lane and snowballs another side.

edits.before: This is where Urgot reclaims it: his Q shotgun legs deal percent-max-HP and his W is sustained DPS that ignores your shields, and once he has items he out-grinds your plateaued damage and executes you with R's fear. Your accumulated tempo from early kills and Starfall roams is your only currency — if the game goes long and even, full-item Urgot beats you straight up. Close it out on your lead before ~2 items, group with Starfall picks, and never trade a sustained fight you can't burst out of.
edits.after: This is where Urgot reclaims it: Purge is sustained damage your shields can't out-heal, Echoing Flames fires off every attack he makes, and Fear Beyond Death impales you and executes below its health threshold. notes: The whole entry is built on a wrong slot. Seven strings call Urgot's leg blasts his Q — 'his shotgun legs (Q)', 'ramping Q legs', 'Q-poke his short legs down'. The legs are Echoing Flames, his passive, and Riot's text is explicit that they fire off his basic attacks and off Purge. His Q, Corrosive Charge, is a ground-targeted explosive that slows. The practical damage is that a player told to trade 'before his Q ramps' is waiting on an ability cooldown that has nothing to do with the damage they are taking. Also removed: four claims that his legs deal percent maximum health. Neither Echoing Flames nor Corrosive Charge mentions percent health anywhere in Riot's text, and the claim actively misdirects itemisation. Added the sequencing rule the mid-game section needed — Purge prioritizes champions Urgot has recently struck with another ability, so eating a Corrosive Charge is what marks you — and the fact that Disdain shields him on the way in, which changes whether trading into his engage is ever correct.
